when.label: Older than the three religions of the region; now mostly on elderly faces

practice.note: Soot mixed with breast milk is the reported ink; a V on the face could say the tribe.

text.what: Kurdistan: marks on women's faces, hands and feet, for protection, for health, and to say which tribe.
text.story: The word comes from Syriac *dyoqo*, puncturing — another tradition that names the tattoo after the movement of the needle. A male tattooist is *deqqak*, a female one *deqqake*; the practice predates Christianity, Yazidism and Islam in the region, and rules attach to it, including who may not receive it.
